assessment: No bench exists, so all ten are pool scouts, ranked by one question: can the engine find it? Seven of ten are legendary and Sisay-fetchable, led by the two mv-0 legendary lands the deck currently has zero of — live targets even at base power 2. The other three (Walking Ballista, Staff of Domination, Aggravated Assault) each convert cards already sleeved into a named combo line. Nearest misses: Freed from the Real (eight lines, but non-legendary and dead without a drawn dork — exactly the blind spot the deck already suffers) and Basalt Monolith (the Kinnan line makes colourless mana, which a {W}{U}{B}{R}{G} activation cannot spend). The obsolescence index's 'upgrades' over Faeburrow Elder (Shang-Chi, Kami of Whispered Hopes, Mona Lisa, Frog Butler) all fail the oracle read — none makes multicoloured mana toward the five-pip activation, so none is on the list.

ten.why: The deck runs zero legendary lands, so a turn-3 Sisay at base power 2 has almost nothing legal to fetch — Cradle is an mv-0 legendary permanent, live at any power, and by midgame it taps for {G} per creature.
ten.unlocks: A guaranteed live fetch on the cold-start turn, plus a Derevi/Emiel line already fully sleeved around it.

ten.why: One card turns the already-sleeved Heliod, Sun-Crowned into the famous two-card kill (45,021 decks run the pair), and at worst it is repeatable removal in a deck holding 2 removal against a budget of 8.
ten.unlocks: A compact kill the toolbox can half-assemble — Sisay fetches Heliod at power 4; Ballista itself is non-legendary and must be drawn, the one thing keeping it out of the top slot.

ten.why: Sisay finds payoffs but not fuel — the deck's draw engines (Rhystic Study, Esper Sentinel) are non-legendary and unfetchable, while The One Ring is a legendary mv-4 draw engine she fetches at power 5; note the 'if you cast it' clause means a fetched Ring skips the protection turn.
ten.unlocks: A tutorable answer to the draw shortfall (6 held against a budget of 10) that also survives every wrath the deck expects.

ten.why: Sisay's activation has no tap symbol, so Minamo's untap points at the battery instead: {U},{T} untaps Jegantha for a second {W}{U}{B}{R}{G} — a second fetch or a Najeela activation in the same turn — and it is itself an mv-0 legendary land, fetchable at any power.
ten.unlocks: Doubled activations on the turn the ladder matures, from a land slot the engine can find on its own.

ten.why: The engine routes entirely through one creature whose loss costs the recast tax plus every ladder rung; the Captain is the same job on a second body — a repeatable legendary tutor, herself fetchable at power 5 — and tutor coverage sits at 1 against a budget of 2.
ten.unlocks: An engine that survives the commander being taxed out of the game.

combo_lines_opened.produces: Infinite untap of legendary creatures you control, infinite mana legendary creatures can produce

ten.why: A legendary combo piece at mv 2 — fetchable at power 3, one colour on board — that borrows the activated abilities of every creature you control, including Ioreth's double untap; the deck's other combo pieces mostly cannot be fetched at all.
ten.unlocks: The Ioreth untap line with both halves inside Sisay's reach, unlike any line the deck currently runs.

ten.why: Recursion sits at 0 against a budget of 2 in a deck whose matchup frame says to assume the wrath; Kethis replays the wiped legends from the graveyard and discounts every legendary recast, and at mv 3 he is fetchable at power 4.
ten.unlocks: A rebuild plan after the sweeper that currently costs the deck its whole ladder.

ten.why: Removal sits at 2 against a budget of 8, and this is the removal the tutor can aim: Sisay's ability is activatable at instant speed, and an Emperor fetched mid-combat entered this turn, so her −2 exiles a tapped attacker on the spot.
ten.unlocks: Tutorable, instant-speed spot removal — the suite's biggest hole filled without spending a drawn card.

combo_lines_opened.produces: Infinite card draw, infinite colored mana

ten.why: Three unverified infinite-draw lines with three separate sleeved dorks (Selvala, Bloom Tender, Faeburrow Elder), and short of the combo it untaps a dork for one more pip toward the five-pip activation.
ten.unlocks: Triple-redundant combo potential over pieces already in the 99 — one Staff, three partners.

combo_lines_opened.produces: Infinite combat phases, infinite colored mana

cards: Esika, God of the Tree // The Prismatic Bridge
combo_lines_opened.produces: Infinite combat phases, infinite untap of creatures

ten.why: The deck's only verified line (stacks/002, Najeela + Derevi) wins through extra combats, and wincons sit at 1 against a budget of 3 — Aggravated Assault is the same wincon class again, with unverified lines through sleeved Selvala and Esika.
ten.unlocks: A second extra-combat engine that shares the pip battery Najeela already taxes, so no new mana ask.

gaps: The claim that a repeatable battlefield tutor justifies one-of silver bullets cannot be cited: the strategy corpus has no toolbox section (best query hit 0.154 per the strategic frame). Until it exists, the removal/recursion picks here rest on the role budget, not on cited construction principle.

Every combo line above is a candidate: Ballista+Heliod, Marvin+Ioreth, Staff+Selvala and Assault+Selvala are the four highest-leverage /resolve-stack scenarios; only stacks/002 (Najeela+Derevi, already fully in-deck) carries a passing checker verdict.

Whether The Wandering Emperor's loyalty can be activated the turn she is fetched mid-combat is read straight off her oracle text ('entered this turn... any time you could cast an instant'), but a stack scenario would make it citable.

The role budget upgrade-facts reports (draw -4, removal -6, recursion -2, sweeper -2, tutor -1, wincon -2) is explicitly provisional and uncited; the sweeper shortfall went unaddressed here — Kagemaro, First to Suffer (legendary, mv 5, tutorable wipe) is the natural eleventh if the pilot weights it higher.
